title: Redstrike Hunt Plan
description: A per-engagement ORDERING + DEPTH-BUDGET plan for the orchestrator's pending-class loop, produced by the Tier-3 `strategist` capability skill from the post-recon state (coverage_ledger.json + surface_ledger.json + the *_context.json feeders + notebook.json + cve_intel.json). It is a RANKING ARTIFACT, not a ledger: it says in which ORDER the already-routed `pending` classes should be hunted and how much DEPTH (beyond the mandatory escalation floor) each is worth, with a rationale. ABSOLUTE INVARIANT — the strategist controls ONLY order and depth-budget: it never marks a class skipped, never writes coverage_ledger.json / surface_ledger.json / any ledger, and can never LOWER the deterministic recall floor. Every class a strategist under-budgets still owes the full escalation ladder (escalation.py), so an under-hunted class still surfaces as a shallow-clear and is caught by the existing recall gate. `coverage.py` remains the SOLE ledger owner. Re-invokable: a later pass re-ranks the REMAINING (not-yet-done) queue as findings arrive.

version.description: hunt_plan schema version (drift guard; bump on a breaking shape change).

iteration.description: 0 = initial post-recon ranking; incremented each re-invocation that re-ranks the remaining queue.

inputs_seen.description: which inputs this pass actually read (e.g. coverage_ledger.json, surface_ledger.json, xss_context.json, notebook.json, cve_intel.json) — an audit trail of what the ranking was based on.

ledger_owner.description: MUST remain 'coverage.py' — a constant assertion that the strategist is NOT the ledger owner and wrote no ledger. Informational; the strategist never touches a ledger regardless of this field.

queue.description: the ranked hunt queue — one entry per routed class the strategist is ordering.

notes.description: free-form strategy rationale for this pass as a whole.

rank.description: 1 = hunt first; the orchestrator iterates its pending-class loop in ascending rank.

class.description: category id, matching routing-map.json / coverage_ledger.json (e.g. xss, sqli, idor).

phase.description: the category's phase (web, ai-llm, ...), copied from the coverage ledger for readability.

queue_state.description: the PLAN's view of this class's position only — NOT a coverage status. queued=not started; in-progress=being hunted; done=hunted (so a re-rank leaves it out of the remaining queue); deferred=ranked last for now (e.g. awaiting a prerequisite finding), still owed in full. 'skipped' is deliberately NOT a value: the strategist can never skip a class — only coverage.py may record a skip, with a reason.

prior.description: the recon prior for this class's surface (feeds escalation.assess). Informational here; it does not change the mandatory floor.

signals.description: the routing signals / evidence that drove this class up or down the ranking.

surface_count.description: how many surface_ledger elements route to this class (a breadth input to the ranking).

severity_ceiling.description: the worst plausible impact if this class lands — a ranking input, never a cap on what is reported.

rationale.description: why this class sits at this rank and budget — the reviewable reasoning.

depth_budget.description: How much DEPTH, BEYOND the mandatory escalation floor, this class is worth. It can only ADD effort, never remove it: even the lowest tier ('floor') means 'run the full deterministic escalation ladder and no more' — it does NOT mean 'do less than the ladder'. The deterministic recall floor (escalation.py + verify-base.md check #5) is unconditional and outside the strategist's control.

tier.description: floor = exhaust the escalation ladder, nothing extra (the minimum; still the full floor); standard = the ladder + proactive parameter-optimization on high-value sinks; deep = the ladder + a diversity pass (different payload set / model) + cross-finding chaining focus. Never below the ladder floor.

min_ladder_steps.description: a hint for the number of escalation-ladder rungs worth trying for this class; a floor-or-above hint only — it can never justify stopping SHORT of the ladder the deterministic recall gate requires.

diversity_pass.description: true (typical for 'deep') = spend budget on a second, differently-seeded pass over the same sinks to raise recall.

rationale.description: why this depth tier (e.g. 'confirmed reflection + CVE-matched component => deep').
